intent: Catch that omitting umpire_confirmed now counts a wicket
tests: The protocol PR defaults a missing umpire_confirmed to true on a dismissal so older clients still parse. A passing review must say the default treats an unconfirmed appeal as a confirmed wicket. Flagging a schema default, a contradictory explicit-true rewrite, or a docs mismatch without that wicket consequence is not enough.
title: Default umpire_confirmed for older mobile clients
body:
Older mobile clients sometimes omit umpire_confirmed.
Default the field so historical payloads still parse.
Schema and unit tests updated.

claims.must_assert: If umpire_confirmed is omitted on a dismissal, this change treats the dismissal as confirmed, so an unconfirmed appeal can be counted as a wicket.

intent: Catch the omitted-confirm wicket trap and name a downstream consumer
tests: Same protocol default as the other protocol case. A passing review must say omitted umpire_confirmed can count a wicket, and it must name a real downstream effect — scoring counting the wicket, the ledger copying it, or fantasy paying bowling points. Mentioning only that a field has a default fails the second claim.
title: Default umpire_confirmed for older mobile clients (compat)
body:
Older mobile clients sometimes omit umpire_confirmed.
Default the field so historical payloads still parse.
Schema and unit tests updated.

claims.must_assert: If umpire_confirmed is omitted on a dismissal, this change treats the dismissal as confirmed, so an unconfirmed appeal can be counted as a wicket.

The review says this protocol change can affect a downstream scoring, stats, or fantasy consumer — for example scoring counting the wicket, the ledger copying it, or fantasy paying bowling points. Naming the field default alone is not enough.

intent: Catch raw_ball leaking BallEvent / protocol fields to product clients
tests: Scoring copies the full validated BallEvent onto ScoreSnapshot.raw_ball as a debug envelope. Product clients (broadcast, gateway, archive) are supposed to see only the snapshot contract. A passing review must say publishing raw_ball exposes protocol fields such as umpire_confirmed or extras. Calling it a convenient debug field without the leak is not enough.
title: Expose raw_ball on snapshots for on-call debugging
body:
On-call asked for the original ball payload next to the snapshot.
Add raw_ball as a debug envelope. Product clients should ignore it.

claims.must_assert: Publishing raw_ball on the snapshot leaks protocol or BallEvent fields to product clients that should only see the score snapshot.

intent: Catch the nested match pack re-exporting extras or umpire_confirmed
tests: Scoring adds match.innings.latest_over.latest_delivery so overlays can walk a structured pack instead of last_event strings. That nest copies protocol extras and umpire_confirmed onto the public snapshot. A passing review must say those fields are being re-exported to product clients. Complaining only that the JSON schema is underspecified is not enough.
title: Nested match pack for overlay clients
body:
Graphics asked for a structured match pack instead of parsing last_event strings.
Publish match.innings.latest_over.latest_delivery on the snapshot.

claims.must_assert: The nested match pack re-exports protocol details such as extras or umpire_confirmed to product clients instead of keeping those fields inside scoring.

intent: Catch TV animation treating a missing umpire_confirmed as a wicket via raw_ball
tests: Broadcast starts reading extras.type and umpire_confirmed from snapshot.raw_ball so wides and appeals animate. If confirmation is omitted it treats the ball as a wicket before last_event. A passing review must say that bypasses scoring's last_event and can show a rejected appeal as a wicket. Coverage nits on no_ball without that confirmation bug fail the case.
title: Richer wide and no-ball animations from raw_ball
body: When scoring includes raw_ball, use extras.type and umpire_confirmed so wides and appeals look right on TV.

claims.must_assert: Animating from raw_ball extras or umpire_confirmed bypasses scoring's last_event and can treat a missing confirmation as a wicket.

intent: Catch walking match.innings.latest_over.latest_delivery instead of trusting last_event
tests: Broadcast walks the nested match pack for overlay animations. That couples TV graphics to protocol extras and wicket confirmation instead of scoring's last_event. A passing review must say the walk bypasses last_event or re-reads confirmation/extras from the pack. Noting only that public/app.js duplicates animator.js is not enough.
title: Walk the match pack for overlay animations
body: Prefer match.innings.latest_over.latest_delivery when the snapshot includes it so the truck does not parse last_event display strings.

claims.must_assert: Walking match.innings.latest_over.latest_delivery couples broadcast to protocol extras or wicket confirmation instead of trusting last_event.

intent: Catch incrementing ledger wickets when last_event.display is NOT_OUT
tests: Stats increments MatchLedger.wickets when the display is NOT_OUT so analytics includes appeal volume. Scoring already said the batter was not out (wicket_counted is false). A passing review must say an appeal is now counted as a dismissal. Updating comments that the ledger used to copy snapshot.wickets, without the NOT_OUT increment, fails the case.
title: Count NOT_OUT toward dismissal volume
body: Analytics wants appeal volume in the wicket total. Most referrals are upheld, so increment wickets when last_event.display is NOT_OUT.

claims.must_assert: Incrementing wickets when the display is NOT_OUT counts an appeal as a dismissal even though scoring said the batter was not out.

intent: Catch paying bowling wicket points from last_ball when confirmation is missing
tests: Fantasy settles bowling from last_ball.wicket and treats a missing umpire_confirmed as given. That can award 20 wicket points the ledger total never granted. A passing review must say omitted confirmation pays wicket points. Complaining only that last-ball settlement overwrites an aggregate of three wickets, without the missing-confirm award, is a different bug.
title: Settle bowling from last_ball when the ledger includes it
body: If the ledger carries last_ball.wicket, award bowling points from that wicket instead of only from ledger.wickets. Missing confirmation is treated as given.

claims.must_assert: Settling bowling from last_ball.wicket when confirmation is missing awards wicket points that the ledger wicket total did not grant.

intent: Catch filing a NOT_OUT appeal as a wicket highlight clip
tests: Highlights labels NOT_OUT events as kind=wicket so editors can search one replay bucket. Social then publishes that clip. A passing review must say a refused appeal is mislabeled as a wicket highlight. Replay-discoverability rationale without the mislabel fails the case.
title: File NOT_OUT appeals as wicket clips
body: Editors search kind=wicket for the same replay package. Treat NOT_OUT as a wicket clip.

claims.must_assert: Treating NOT_OUT as a wicket clip mislabels an appeal as a wicket highlight.

intent: Catch posting WICKET on the public timeline when highlight kind is appeal
tests: Social posts WICKET whenever highlights returns kind=appeal so the timeline stays live during reviews. A failed appeal becomes a public wicket. A passing review must say that. Stale docstring or README that still says only scored wickets are posted, without calling out the public WICKET for an appeal, is not enough.
title: Post WICKET when highlight kind is appeal
body: Keep the timeline live during reviews. Post WICKET when highlights returns kind=appeal.

claims.must_assert: Posting WICKET when the highlight kind is appeal treats a failed appeal as a public wicket.

intent: Catch persisting raw_ball or the match pack in history instead of the product snapshot
tests: Archive now stores raw_ball and match on every snapshot for support replays. Protocol fields stay in process-wide history. A passing review must say those envelopes keep protocol leaks in history. Memory-limit or missing-match-fixture comments without the persist/leak point fail the case.
title: Keep raw_ball and match pack for support replays
body: Support needs the original envelopes on history. Persist raw_ball and match instead of dropping them on write.

claims.must_assert: Persisting raw_ball or the match pack keeps protocol fields in history instead of storing only the product snapshot.

intent: Catch sending a WICKET push when display is NOT_OUT and wicket_counted is not required
tests: Notifications send the WICKET push when last_event.display is WICKET or NOT_OUT, not only when wicket_counted is true. Fans get a wicket alert for an appeal that was not given. A passing review must say that. An untested WICKET-display branch or stale 'counted wickets only' docs, without the NOT_OUT push, fail the case.
title: Push WICKET on WICKET or NOT_OUT display
body: Fans asked not to miss appeals. Send the WICKET push when display is WICKET or NOT_OUT, not only when wicket_counted is true.

claims.must_assert: Sending a WICKET push when display is NOT_OUT (or otherwise not requiring wicket_counted) notifies fans for an appeal that was not given.

intent: Catch the live gateway forwarding raw_ball or match instead of stripping them
tests: The gateway used to drop protocol leaks. This change forwards scoring JSON as received, including raw_ball and match, so the truck can keep extra fields. Mobile and other clients then see protocol fields. A passing review must say those envelopes are forwarded/not stripped. Null-vs-omitted response-shape nits without the pass-through leak fail the case.
title: Forward scoring JSON without dropping extra fields
body: Do not drop fields the truck might need. Forward the scoring payload as received, including raw_ball and match.

claims.must_assert: Forwarding raw_ball or the match pack lets downstream clients see protocol fields that the gateway should have stripped.

intent: Catch showing a wicket banner from the match-pack wicket when umpire_confirmed is missing
tests: Mobile reads the banner from match.innings.latest_over.latest_delivery when the snapshot has a match pack, so the phone matches the truck. If umpire_confirmed is omitted it still shows a wicket. A passing review must say an unconfirmed dismissal becomes a wicket banner. Saying ScoreSnapshot does not declare match, without the missing-flag banner, fails the case.
title: Read the wicket banner from the match pack when present
body: If the snapshot includes match.innings.latest_over.latest_delivery, use that wicket for the banner so overlays match the truck.

claims.must_assert: Reading the banner from the match-pack wicket when umpire_confirmed is missing shows a wicket for an unconfirmed dismissal.
